shots.name: Shooter Lane
shots.notes: Both a soft and a hard plunge are available. On the Pro the hard plunge is the skill shot; on Premium and LE a hard plunge feeds the upper playfield once per ball instead.

shots.name: Top Lanes
shots.notes: Two lanes across the top. Completing the pair raises the bonus multiplier, which caps at 20x. On the Pro each completion also counts toward Battle at the Wall.

shots.name: Pop Bumpers
shots.notes: Stern's reel-style bumpers. Rattling around up here spins a set of awards you can bank and cash whenever you like — extra mode time, bonus multiplier, gold, Wildfire, Advance Wall, Light Sword, even Add-A-Ball.

shots.name: Left Drop Target 3-Bank
shots.notes: Clearing all three bumps the spinner up a level and, once per game, lights Lord of Light. Three completions qualify House Baratheon.

shots.name: Left Loop
shots.notes: Backhandable off the left flipper. Three of them qualify House Greyjoy. On Premium and LE the gates near the bumpers often hand you a second loop for free.

shots.name: Left Loop Spinner
shots.notes: Nine value levels, but the level is capped at the number of house modes you have finished plus one, and it drops back to level one at the start of every ball.

shots.name: Dragon Lane
shots.notes: A kicker lane with a post that can trap the ball. On the Pro this is Mystery, extra ball and the Battle at the Wall start. Three shots qualify House Targaryen.

shots.name: Castle Black
shots.notes: The longer kicker lane that replaces the Dragon's multiball duty on Premium and LE. Six shots here enable Battle at the Wall; it also qualifies House Targaryen in three.

shots.name: Left Ramp
shots.notes: The most important shot on the machine. It locks for Blackwater, starts every house battle, and starts both wizard modes. Usually taken from the right flipper. Three of them qualify House Lannister.

shots.name: Battering Ram
shots.notes: Where playfield multipliers are built, where Wildfire is collected, and where every Super Jackpot in the game is cashed. Watch the blue arrow in front of it — while it flashes, your next ram hit advances the multiplier.

shots.name: Gold Standup Targets
shots.notes: Your gold supply, and the way to light Mystery. You will hit these by accident all game, which is why Lannister's gold bonus is quietly strong.

shots.name: Right Ramp
shots.notes: House Stark's shot and the Sword collect. Backhandable from the right flipper. On the Pro it returns to the left flipper; on Premium and LE it feeds the upper playfield.

shots.name: Right Target 2-Bank
shots.notes: House Tyrell's shot. Completing the pair lights a Blackwater lock and lights Wildfire.

shots.name: Right Loop
shots.notes: House Martell's shot. On the Pro it does nothing else; on Premium and LE it feeds the Iron Throne and takes over Mystery, extra ball and the Wall multiball start.

shots.name: Iron Throne
shots.notes: The throne toy fed by the right loop. It is the collect point for Mystery and extra ball on these cabinets.

shots.name: Upper Playfield
shots.notes: Two flippers, three touch targets, two back lanes that drop into the left loop, and a castle mini-loop. The wire gate up here also spots right ramp shots if you clip it hard enough.

shots.name: Upper Playfield Targets
shots.notes: A centre target flanked by two outer ones. During a mode each hit in the centre-outer-centre sequence buys you 5 seconds and eventually lights the castle loop.

shots.name: Castle Loop
shots.notes: The mini-loop on the upper playfield. Collecting the castle during a mode is worth 15 million up front plus 7.5 million in bonus, which is a lot for a shot most players ignore.

shots.name: Action Button
shots.notes: Your house power lives here. It is solidly lit in your house colour when it is ready, and for most houses it is one use per ball.

shots.name: Left Inlane
shots.notes: Raises the combo multiplier when lit. Playing Tyrell keeps one inlane lit permanently, and lane change moves which one.

shots.name: Right Inlane
shots.notes: The other half of the combo multiplier pair. During Hand of the King both inlanes flash and a roll-through pulls every shot up to your best current multiplier.

shots.name: Left Outlane
shots.notes: Covered by Lord of Light when it is lit, and by Baratheon's action button power.

shots.name: Right Outlane
shots.notes: Same protection as the left. Specials pay 25 million here when a Mystery award hands you one.

shots.name: Upper Playfield Left Flipper
shots.notes: One of the upper playfield's two flippers, confirmed to exist but not individually documented; side/position/size estimated.

shots.name: Upper Playfield Right Flipper
shots.notes: The second of the upper playfield's two flippers; side/position/size estimated.

goals.title: Lit Lane Skill Shot
goals.summary: On the Pro, hard plunge into the lit top lane. It pays 500,000 multiplied by the ball number, so it is worth more on ball three than ball one, and it hands you a bonus multiplier on top.
goals.reward: 500K x ball number, plus 1 bonus X

steps.action: Plunge hard into the lit lane
steps.detail: Playfield validation happens on a rollover, so a soft plunge that dies short does not count. Premium and LE cabinets have no skill shot at all — there, a hard plunge feeds the upper playfield once per ball.

goals.title: Choose Your House
goals.summary: The first decision of the game and the one that shapes everything after it. Your house gives you a permanent perk plus an action button power, and the house you pick is immediately qualified to battle.
goals.reward: A persistent perk and an action button power
instructions: Stark: adds 10 million to every Winter is Coming hurry-up. The button sends the direwolf to finish your current battle instantly for a flat 5 million — a way to rush the wizard modes, not to score.
Baratheon: starts you two advances into Battle at the Wall and raises its jackpots. The button buys a short ball save on both outlanes.
Lannister: roughly 1.5x gold from the standups and 500 gold to open. The button buys the next playfield multiplier level outright at 600 gold per level, capped at eight uses per game.
Greyjoy: starts already completed, and you inherit the perk of every house you beat. The cost is that each battle needs more shots and you can only fight one house at a time.
Tyrell: keeps one inlane lit for combo multiplier at all times, which is worth far more than it sounds. The button cashes the Iron Bank, trading your playfield and combo multipliers for a lump sum.
Martell: no perk, but the button is an add-a-ball in any multiball.
Targaryen: its whole three-level battle is spotted complete for free. The button freezes every running timer for 15 seconds.
You can also buy a Baratheon, Martell or Lannister button power from the Mystery menu later for around 3,800 gold; it replaces your current one for the rest of the game.

goals.title: Qualify And Start House Battles
goals.summary: Every house owns a shot. Hit that shot three times to qualify the house, then take the left ramp when mode start is lit to begin the battle. Battles run 40 seconds — 30 for Martell, just 15 for Greyjoy — and most are worth restarting rather than abandoning.
goals.reward: Mode scoring, plus progress toward both wizard modes

steps.action: Work each house's shot three times
steps.detail: Drops qualify Baratheon, left loop Greyjoy, Dragon or Castle Black Targaryen, left ramp Lannister, right ramp Stark, right loop Martell, right 2-bank Tyrell.
With two or more qualified you can stack a pair, unless you are playing Greyjoy. You may also pass, but then you need a new house or a third Blackwater lock to relight the start.
A timed-out battle does not need requalifying — just shoot the ramp again. Lannister, Greyjoy, Tyrell and Targaryen keep the progress you already made.

goals.title: What Each Battle Wants
goals.summary: Seven battles, seven different jobs. Knowing the objective before the timer starts is the difference between a completed house and a wasted 40 seconds.
goals.reward: Four houses lights Hand of the King, all seven lights Iron Throne
instructions: Stark: build the kill list on the ramps, then cash it on an orbit. Three ramps first, or one if you are restarting a failed attempt. 40 seconds.

Baratheon: build value with the spinner from either orbit, then hit the Dragon it lights — the Dragon is what qualifies the cash-in on the left drop bank, signalled by the flashing shield. 40 seconds.
Lannister: gold targets light the two shots adjacent to them and raise their value. Five lit shots finishes it. 40 seconds, and progress carries if you fail.
Greyjoy: every major shot is lit and you have 15 seconds, refreshed on each completed shot. Fast and unforgiving.
Tyrell: lit shots alternate between the ramps and Dragon and the lock targets. Hit a lit shot, hit the target bank, then the ramps come back — and by the third cycle only the right ramp is left.
Martell: three orbits inside a 10-second window that refreshes after the second, then either ramp for the hurry-up. The final ramp is bonus points only; the three orbits alone finish the battle.

Targaryen: three escalating dragons, each a set of lit shots followed by the Dragon lane. Level three lights three hurry-up shots at a time and punishes slow play by resetting the wave with a harder set.
Playing Greyjoy adds requirements to every battle — usually every shot and both target banks — so budget more time for each one.

goals.title: Winter Is Coming
goals.summary: Every time you qualify a house, the shot you used to qualify it ices over. Freeze three shots and the hurry-up starts. Collect four hurry-ups across the game and you go straight into the mini wizard mode.
goals.reward: A hurry-up value, and progress to Winter Has Come

steps.detail: Any three of the seven — both target banks, both ramps, both loops and the Dragon — and they do not have to be different shots.
It is always the last shot you froze. Nothing else scores progress while the hurry-up runs except locks, outlane lights and multiball starts.
Starting a hurry-up on the mode-start ramp with your third Blackwater lock lit launches multiball with no chance to pick a house to stack. Clear that shot's hurry-up before you light the third lock.

goals.title: Winter Has Come
goals.summary: Bank four Winter is Coming hurry-ups and this fires off at once: four balls in play, two phases that alternate. Jackpot scoring comes from the hurry-up values you banked earlier, which is why Stark's perk can make the mode enormous.
goals.reward: Super Jackpot pays out all four banked hurry-up values again

steps.detail: All seven major shots are lit on a hidden timer. Each one restarts the clock; letting it expire adds another shot. Listen for the ticking, because it is not on the display.
Three shots run their own hurry-ups. Let one expire and your left flipper freezes until you make the ramp with your right.

steps.action: Collect five shots for the Super
steps.detail: It re-awards every Winter is Coming hurry-up value you have banked, then throws you back to the Horde for another run.
Start your fourth hurry-up on a shot that will not launch a multiball, then start the multiball you want while it counts down, and collect the hurry-up inside it.

goals.title: Blackwater Multiball
goals.summary: The bread-and-butter multiball. Complete the right 2-bank to light a lock, then lock at the left ramp — and you must lock before you can light the next one. Three locks starts it.
goals.reward: Jackpots on the five major shots, Super Jackpot at the ram

steps.detail: The first lock needs only one of the two green targets; the second needs both individually; the third and later need both completed on a timer once the first is hit.
Each lock also hands you 5 Wildfire, which raises the jackpots you are about to shoot for.

steps.action: Complete the five shots, then bash the ram
steps.detail: You get a 20-second window on the Super and no cap on repeats, so keep pounding the ram for as long as it holds — and every one of those hits feeds your playfield multiplier too.
Letting the Super expire relights the jackpots needing two shots each, then three, each round worth more but harder to finish.

goals.title: Battle At The Wall
goals.summary: A three-ball multiball earned by grinding one repetitive shot. On the Pro that is six top lane completions; on Premium and LE it is six shots to Castle Black. The second one costs eleven.
goals.reward: Ramp and loop jackpots, Super Jackpot on the Dragon

steps.detail: Pro players complete the top lanes six times; Premium and LE players shoot Castle Black six times. Playing Baratheon, a completed drop bank also spots one.
The Dragon starts it on the Pro, the right loop on Premium and LE.
Three ramp jackpots light the Super on the Dragon; the jackpots then move to the loops, and three loops relight the Dragon again.

goals.title: Castle Multiball
goals.summary: The upper playfield's own multiball on Premium and LE, and the one most players never deliberately go for. Progress comes in four named steps and each one raises a drop target that blocks your right ramp until you clear it.
goals.reward: A separate multiball earned entirely upstairs

steps.detail: All three upstairs, in any order.
That banks one step. The four steps are Archers, Charge, Breach and finally Castle Multiball.
Every step raises a drop target in front of the right ramp. Shoot the target to drop it, or start any mode or multiball, which drops it for you.

goals.title: Hand Of The King
goals.summary: Complete four houses while you are not in a battle and the mode start lights for it. It plays in sets: light shots, complete them, then cash a Super at the ram. Which four houses you bring changes the mode more than anything else you do.
goals.reward: Super Jackpots built from your best four shots per set

steps.action: Start it with four houses banked
steps.detail: You must not be in a battle when the fourth completes, or it will not light.
Four shots per set, or seven if you brought Baratheon. Every shot value also feeds the Super.
A roll-through adds 1x to the combo multiplier and pulls every shot up to your best current level — this works here whether or not you are playing Tyrell, and can push combos to 6x.
It is built from your best four shots of the set. Three completed sets, or two if you brought Greyjoy, start a much larger hurry-up at the ram.

goals.title: Iron Throne
goals.summary: The full wizard mode, and it takes all seven houses. What makes it unusual is that it does not end — not when you drain to one ball, and not when your ball ends. You pick it back up on the next ball.
goals.reward: Super Jackpot plus an add-a-ball per castle taken

steps.detail: Every house light goes out and the mode opens as a two-ball multiball with all house shots lit.

steps.action: Take all seven shots in a set
steps.detail: Shots switch off as you make them. The shot belonging to the castle you are currently besieging is lit in that house's colour and pays far more.

steps.action: Cash the Super and add a ball
steps.detail: Completing a set lights the ram for a Super plus an add-a-ball, and raises that house's shield to mark it done.
Shoot any remaining unlit house shot. After the last castle falls you get one more ball and a run of victory-lap shots until you are back down to one.

goals.title: Playfield Multiplier
goals.summary: Three hits to the battering ram qualify the multiplier and a fourth starts it. Every four hits after that adds another 1x, up to 5x — but the higher it goes, the shorter it lasts.
goals.reward: 2x through 5x on all playfield scoring

steps.detail: After the first ram hit the arrow in front of it flashes. Advance while it flashes or the progress lapses and you have to relight it, which is why a 3-hit ladder can cost you six.
With Wildfire lit at the ram, each multiplier level costs only three hits instead of four.

steps.action: Cash it before you lose it
steps.detail: The action button converts your multipliers into points. The disciplined play is to press it as the ball is draining rather than letting the timer eat them.

goals.title: Combo Multiplier
goals.summary: A second multiplier that lives on individual shots rather than the whole playfield. Making shots raises other shots' multipliers, and rolling a lit inlane pushes them along faster. It caps at 5x under normal play.
goals.reward: Up to 5x on individual shot values

steps.detail: Playing Tyrell keeps one lit permanently and lane change lets you pick which — a small-sounding perk that pays off in every timed battle.
Each made shot raises the multipliers waiting on the others, so a clean run around the playfield compounds.

goals.title: Collect Swords
goals.summary: Finish a house battle and the right ramp lights for a Sword. Swords are worth points on their own, but the real reason to collect them is that each one raises the ceiling on your playfield multiplier.
goals.reward: Raises the playfield multiplier cap from 3x toward 5x

steps.detail: A pop bumper award can also light a Sword.
Without swords your playfield multiplier stops at 3x. Each sword adds 1x to that ceiling up to 5x; beyond that they are pure points, and they multiply well.

goals.title: Wildfire
goals.summary: Complete the lock targets to light Wildfire at the ram, then keep hitting it. The first hit gives 10, and each hit after gives one more than the last. Wildfire raises your Blackwater jackpots, though with diminishing returns as the pile grows.
goals.reward: Bigger Blackwater jackpots, and cheaper playfield multipliers

steps.detail: A pop bumper or Mystery award can also hand you the mini-mode outright, or 5 Wildfire on its own.
10, then 11, then 12 and up. Wildfire lit at the ram also drops each playfield multiplier level from four hits to three.

goals.title: Gold And The Mystery Shop
goals.summary: Complete the gold standups to light Mystery, then choose between keeping your gold and two priced awards. The menu is a genuine shop with fixed prices, so gold is a currency worth managing rather than a scoring stat.
goals.reward: Anything from 1 million to a lit extra ball

steps.detail: Playing Lannister these pay around 1.5x, which is what makes the expensive end of the menu reachable.
The Dragon on the Pro, the right loop on Premium and LE.
Cheap and useful: 1 million for 120, light a house for 140, a bonus multiplier for 160, light lock for 250. The big end: light extra ball at 4,500 and 25 million at 6,000.

goals.title: Lord Of Light
goals.summary: Clearing the left drop bank arms a ball save on both outlanes — but by default only once for the entire game. Treat it as a single insurance policy and think about when you want it active.
goals.reward: A save on both outlanes

steps.detail: The completion also advances your spinner a level, so it is never a wasted shot.
Once it is spent, further Lord of Light awards only come from a pop bumper or the Mystery shop.

goals.title: The Spinner Ladder
goals.summary: Nine levels of spinner value, with one hard rule attached: you can never climb higher than the number of house modes you have completed plus one. It also resets to level one at the start of every ball.
goals.reward: A spinner that actually scores

steps.action: Complete the drop bank to level up
steps.detail: Each individual drop target hit also raises the spinner's value inside the current level.
The higher the level, the faster the value grows. Since it resets every ball, this is a within-ball investment, not a long game.
Ram hits sometimes raise the spinner value as well.

goals.title: Build The Bonus Multiplier
goals.summary: The top lanes drive a bonus multiplier that climbs all the way to 20x — high enough to be worth real points on a long ball, and on the Pro every completion doubles as progress toward Battle at the Wall.
goals.reward: Bonus multiplier up to 20x

steps.detail: On the Pro this is also one of your six Wall multiball advances, so it is never a wasted trip.
Bumper awards and Mystery awards both hand out bonus multipliers, sometimes three at a time.

goals.title: Working The Upper Playfield
goals.summary: On Premium and LE the upper playfield is not decoration during a battle — it is a time machine. Each target in the right sequence buys 5 seconds, and the castle at the end pays 15 million plus 7.5 million in bonus.
goals.reward: Mode time, 15M and 7.5M bonus per castle

steps.detail: A lit centre target lights the outer ones and adds 5 seconds; an outer target relights the centre for another 5; the centre again adds 5 more and lights the castle.
What it does next depends on your battle — Stark and Lannister get an advance, Baratheon and Martell build their jackpot or hurry-up, Greyjoy and Tyrell get back lanes that spot a lit shot.

goals.title: Turn Off Casual Mode
goals.summary: Some machines are set up in a stripped-down mode that takes your house choice away and starts you as Stark. You can refuse it from the cabinet before the game even begins.
goals.reward: Full rules, including choosing your own house
instructions: Hold the right flipper button for about three seconds before you start the game and it will boot into full rules instead.
To check a machine you do not know, flip through the attract mode first: if one of the screens explains how to enable advanced play, casual mode is on.
Under casual mode you start as Stark with Stark already complete and Greyjoy lit, you cannot pass on a battle, and a single lit house starts without asking.
The operator's difficulty, home and director's cut settings all change this, so a machine you played last week may not behave the same today.

achievements.title: Take The Black
achievements.desc: Hard plunge into the lit lane for the skill shot.

achievements.title: Bend The Knee
achievements.desc: Qualify a house and start your first battle at the left ramp.

achievements.title: The Night Is Dark
achievements.desc: Clear the left drop bank to arm Lord of Light on the outlanes.

achievements.title: Blackwater
achievements.desc: Lock three balls at the left ramp and start Blackwater Multiball.

achievements.title: Hold The Wall
achievements.desc: Bank six advances and start Battle at the Wall.

achievements.title: Green Fire
achievements.desc: Light Wildfire and collect it at the battering ram.

achievements.title: Winter Is Coming
achievements.desc: Freeze three shots and collect a Winter is Coming hurry-up.

achievements.title: Bring The Ram
achievements.desc: Climb the playfield multiplier to 5x using Sword collects.

achievements.title: Winter Has Come
achievements.desc: Collect four hurry-ups and reach the four-ball mini wizard mode.

achievements.title: Hand Of The King
achievements.desc: Complete four houses and start Hand of the King.

achievements.title: The Iron Throne
achievements.desc: Complete all seven houses and start the Iron Throne wizard mode.

achievements.title: Breach The Gate
achievements.desc: Work the upper playfield through Archers, Charge and Breach to Castle Multiball.

drills.title: Hard Plunge, Lit Lane
drills.text: On the Pro, playfield validation happens on a rollover, so a soft plunge that dies short scores nothing at all. Drive the ball into the lit top lane and save your best attempts for later balls, since the award multiplies by the ball number; Premium and LE have no skill shot, and a hard plunge feeds the upper playfield instead.

drills.title: Own The Left Ramp
drills.text: This one shot locks for Blackwater, starts every house battle and starts both wizard modes, and it is usually taken from the right flipper. Drill it until it is automatic, because a game where you cannot make it is a game with no modes in it.

drills.title: Ram While The Arrow Flashes
drills.text: After the first ram hit, the blue arrow in front of it flashes and only hits inside that flash advance the multiplier. Take the whole ladder in one visit — let the arrow lapse and a three-hit climb quietly costs you six.

drills.title: Steer The Lit Inlane
drills.text: Move the lit inlane onto the side the ball is actually returning down, using lane change before it gets there. Every roll-through raises the combo multiplier waiting on the other shots, which is what makes a clean lap around the playfield compound.

drills.title: Five Shots, Then The Ram
drills.text: In Blackwater, clear the five jackpot shots and go straight to the battering ram for the Super — there is no cap on repeats inside the twenty-second window, so keep pounding it while it holds. Letting the Super expire relights the jackpots needing two shots each, then three.

drills.title: Freeze Three, Then Collect
drills.text: The flashing white hurry-up shot is always the last shot you froze, so know which one that was before it starts. Clear a hurry-up sitting on the mode-start ramp before you light your third lock, or the multiball launches with no chance to stack a house into it.

actionButton.label: Action Button
actionButton.how: This button is the whole reason your opening house choice matters. Each house hands you a permanent perk plus one power that fires from the lockdown bar, and the button glows solid in your house colour when that power is charged. For most houses it recharges once per ball, so treat every press as a decision rather than a reflex.

uses.when: Ball heading down with multipliers running
uses.what: Converts your playfield and combo multipliers into points. Press as it drains instead of watching the timer eat them.
Sends the direwolf to finish the running house battle instantly for a flat 5 million. Progress toward the wizard modes, not points.
Buys the next playfield multiplier level outright at 600 gold per level, capped at eight presses per game.
Freezes every running timer for 15 seconds. Ball-save timers keep counting down regardless.
Buys a short ball save on both outlanes, timed from roughly your next switch hit.

howItPlays.objective: Swear to one of seven houses, then win its battles across the realm while stacking Blackwater and Wall multiballs. Conquer four houses for Hand of the King and all seven to seize the Iron Throne.
loop: Open by pledging to a house; that pick hands you a lasting perk and a lockdown-bar power in your own colors.
Pound a house's own shot three times to ready it, then take the left ramp when start is lit to open the battle.
Feed the battering ram to grow your playfield multiplier, and lock at the left ramp off the right target pair for Blackwater.
Each house you finish arms a Sword and inches you up the wizard ladder; four opens Hand of the King, seven crowns the Iron Throne.

lights.name: House Battle Shots
lights.lit: Every house claims one shot -- the left drops, the left loop, the Dragon, both ramps, the right loop and the right target pair -- and three hits on that shot readies its battle.
lights.flashing: A readied house flashes the left ramp for mode start; bank a pair of them and you can open both battles stacked together.
lights.then: Start at the left ramp, clear that house's particular job inside its timer, and a Sword lights at the right ramp. Time out and you simply re-shoot the ramp to try again -- several houses even keep the progress you already made.

lights.name: Blackwater Locks
lights.lit: Finishing the green pair on the right lights a lock at the left ramp, and until you cash that lit lock the next one stays dark; each lock also drops a fistful of Wildfire in your pocket.
lights.then: Sink three locks to erupt Blackwater, then sweep the five major shots and pound the ram for an uncapped Super while the window holds. Every one of those ram hits feeds your playfield multiplier at the same time.

lights.name: Battering Ram Multiplier
lights.lit: A blue arrow flares in front of the ram after your first hit, and only a ram strike taken while it flares steps the playfield multiplier up; let the arrow go dark and the rung lapses, so a three-hit climb can quietly cost you six.
lights.flashing: While the arrow flares, your next strike on the ram bumps the multiplier a rung; with Wildfire burning there, each rung costs a hit less.
lights.then: Drive the multiplier from doubled scoring up toward its ceiling, and collect Swords off finished battles to lift that ceiling higher. Bank the whole stack into points with your house power before a drain or the timer swallows it.

lights.name: Combo Multiplier Inlanes
lights.lit: One return lane glows for the combo multiplier at a time; rolling the lit one lifts the multiplier waiting on your other shots, and pledging to Tyrell simply keeps one lit the whole game.
lights.flashing: Both returns strobe during Hand of the King, when one roll hauls all of your shots to the top level you have reached so far.

control.effect: a tap of a flipper button jumps the lit return over to the opposite side, so you can drop it onto whichever rail the ball is truly coming down and never waste the roll
control.when: as the ball heads back toward the return lanes

lights.then: Steer the lit return under the ball, roll it, and watch the shot multipliers climb toward their cap; a clean lap of the playfield compounds because each made shot seeds the next. During Hand of the King that same roll snaps everything up to your top level at once.

lights.name: Winter Is Coming Frozen Shots
lights.lit: Any shot you used to ready a house freezes over behind you; ice three of them and a white hurry-up ignites on the last one you froze.
lights.flashing: The flashing white shot is always that last frozen one -- almost nothing else banks progress while its hurry-up ticks.
lights.then: Cash the white shot for its hurry-up, and stow four of these across the game to drop straight into Winter Has Come, a four-ball storm whose Super repays every hurry-up you banked. Bank any hurry-up parked on the start ramp before a third lock lights there, or the multiball fires off with no house to stack in.

lights.name: Bonus Multiplier Top Lanes
lights.lit: The back lanes drive your end-of-ball bonus multiplier; finish the pair and it climbs, all the way to a ceiling that adds up to real money once a ball runs long.
lights.then: Complete the lanes to step the bonus up, and pocket the free ones the reel bumpers and the Mystery menu toss out, sometimes several at once. On a Pro every completion also counts as one of your advances toward the Wall multiball, so a trip up top is never wasted.

lights.name: Gold and Mystery
lights.lit: The gold standups are both your treasury and the way to arm Mystery; you clip them all game by accident, which is what makes Lannister's boosted gold quietly strong.
lights.then: Finish the gold to light Mystery at the Dragon -- the right loop instead on Premium and LE -- then spend at a fixed-price shop that runs from a cheap million up to a lit extra ball. Treat gold as a currency to hoard for the dear end of the menu, not a stat to watch tick by.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Tap either flipper button to jump the lit combo-multiplier insert to the opposite return lane, so you can steer it onto the rail the ball is coming down. Roll the lit return to raise the multiplier waiting on your other shots (Tyrell keeps one lit permanently), and during Hand of the King a single roll lifts all of your shots to the top level you have earned at once.

scoring.text: Pick the house whose style fits how you shoot, since that choice colors the entire game, and clear the left drop bank early to bank Lord of Light as one-shot outlane insurance. Learn the left ramp cold -- it starts every battle and both wizard modes.
Grow the score with multiball and multipliers. Lock three for Blackwater, grind the Wall multiball, ladder the ram up to a fat playfield multiplier, and stow Winter is Coming hurry-ups for later.

Finish four houses out of battle to open Hand of the King, and bank four hurry-ups for the Winter Has Come storm. Conquer all seven houses for the Iron Throne, the crown of the game -- a siege that refuses to end, carrying on ball after ball until the last castle falls.
